newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine unions and business leaders to meet.
newsitem.headline: Argentine unions and business leaders to meet.

text.p: Argentina's "Group of Eight" business lobby and the CGT labor federation were due to meet at 1700 local time/1500 EST Tuesday to hammer out a preliminary agreement on employment and labor reforms.

After debate among businessmen had threatened Monday to derail Tuesday's scheduled talks, the group of Argentina's eight biggest business chambers confirmed the talks would go ahead and both sides said the prospects were good.

"There is a good chance of nearing agreement and the differences are not very large," said Jorge Di Fiori, head of the Argentine Chamber of Commerce. "It would have sent the wrong signal to society not to go."
On the union side, construction leader Gerardo Martinez, a CGT director, told state news agency Telam:

"The businessmen have some internal conflicts based on differences of position, but the idea is that in today's meeting we will try and make the way forward easier and consolidate some of the common ground we already have."

Peronist President Carlos Menem is urging both sides to hurry an agreement on how to tackle Argentina's high jobless rate of 17.3 percent. The government and unions, once allies, have been fighting over Menem's attempts to modernize labor laws by decree -- currently stalled in the courts.

Menem, who had promised to go to the Supreme Court to get his labor decrees applied, agreed with the unions on a truce in the legal battle ending March 12, in order to ease the way for the talks between unions and business leaders.
